summary: ETH Zürich's Excellence Scholarship & Opportunity Programme (ESOP) funds about 60 outstanding master's students a year at one of the world's leading science and engineering universities. It pays living costs and waives tuition for the whole master's.
covers: A living allowance of CHF 13,500 per semester for students starting in autumn 2027 (CHF 12,000 before then).
A full tuition-fee waiver for the standard length of the master's (three or four semesters).
About 60 scholarships were available for students starting in 2027/28.
eligibility: Applicants to an ETH master's programme, from any university in the world.
Outstanding bachelor's results — ETH asks for the top 10% of your cohort (grade A).
You must not already be enrolled in, or hold, a master's degree.
how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme and ESOP together through ETH's eApply portal.
Upload a pre-proposal for your master's thesis research as part of the scholarship application.
Name two professors as referees if your programme does not already require recommendation letters; they submit letters directly.
Submit between 1 and 30 November 2026 (11:59 pm Swiss time) for a start in autumn 2027. Decisions are communicated by the end of March.
watch_out: The ESOP window closes on 30 November — two weeks before ETH's regular master's deadline of mid-December. Apply in November to be considered for the scholarship.
Being in the top 10% is necessary but not sufficient; the thesis pre-proposal and references carry real weight.
Zürich is among the most expensive cities in Europe; the allowance is set to cover a modest student budget there, not luxuries.
